sources.title: qwen-turbo model information
sources.evidence: Rechecked October 27, 2026. The official English page remains in the search index and identifies the Qwen3 Turbo alias as functionally equivalent to qwen-turbo-2025-04-28. It says reasoning rivals QwQ-32B with a smaller parameter size, but publishes no nominal total or active count and names no sized base model. Direct opening redirects to the general models page. The indexed card still documents 131072-token context, text input/output, optional thinking and unsupported Function Calling.

sources.title: Qwen Key Concepts
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Identifies Qwen as an Alibaba Group model family and explicitly lists Qwen Turbo among proprietary language models, separately from open-weight checkpoints. It does not disclose a Turbo parameter count or name a sized base model.

sources.title: Qwen2.5: A Party of Foundation Models!
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The September 19, 2024 announcement already offers Qwen-Turbo through Model Studio APIs. Published sizes and dense architecture apply to separately listed open-weight models; the post does not give Turbo a nominal size or identify a named sized base.

sources.title: Extending the Context Length to 1M Tokens!
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The November 15, 2024 announcement describes the older Qwen2.5-Turbo revision, a context extension from 128k to 1M and sparse attention. It supplies neither a parameter count nor an explicit relationship to a sized base; it cannot establish the later Qwen3 snapshot architecture or size.

sources.title: Notice on the Decommissioning of Certain Historical Mainline Models
sources.evidence: Official notice schedules qwen-turbo decommissioning in Beijing and Singapore for October 10, 2026; inference calls cease after decommissioning. No API execution was performed during this audit.

sources.title: Output price of Qwen-Plus and Qwen-Turbo reduced under Qwen3 thinking mode
sources.evidence: July 14, 2025 announcement explicitly lists thinking-mode pricing for Qwen-Turbo and Qwen-Turbo-2025-04-28, effective July 18.

sources.title: qwen-turbo 模型信息
sources.evidence: Fresh Chinese-language primary-source search on October 27, 2026 found the indexed card, updated September 11, 2026, explicitly equating qwen-turbo with the qwen-turbo-2025-04-28 snapshot. Its size statement only compares reasoning with QwQ-32B using a smaller parameter scale; it does not report total or active counts or a named-base relationship. Direct opening redirects to the general models page.

sources.title: Qwen3: Think Deeper, Act Faster
sources.evidence: Reopened April 29, 2025 developer release on October 27, 2026. Explicit nominal sizes include Qwen3-30B-A3B at 30B total and 3B activated, Qwen3-235B-A22B at 235B total and 22B activated, and six named dense models. The post does not mention Turbo or identify it as a variant of any sized model. Its QwQ-32B comparison is not evidence that Turbo is Qwen3-30B-A3B.

sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio: Model lifecycle and updates
sources.evidence: Opened the current lifecycle page and checked the indexed June 24, 2025 qwen-turbo entry on October 27, 2026. The entry calls it a Qwen3-series Turbo model and repeats the smaller-size comparison with QwQ-32B. No nominal total, activated count, or explicit lineage to a sized model is disclosed. This adds a separate official release-history check to the indexed exact-model card.

sources.title: Original Qwen DashScope documentation listing qwen-turbo (October 16, 2023)
sources.evidence: The October 16, 2023 immutable README names qwen-turbo and qwen-plus as available DashScope hosted APIs, distinguishes their speed/quality and provides API-key onboarding plus SDK installation instructions. It establishes that qwen-turbo existed by October 16, 2023 without claiming an original release date.

sources.title: Qwen original API documentation commit metadata
sources.evidence: The official repository commit is timestamped October 16, 2023. Inspection of earlier October 14 README and this revision locates the documentation addition; a documentation commit timestamp alone does not establish the model launch date.

developer.note: Qwen Team is part of Alibaba Group.

family.note: Broad family retained; this hosted alias later used Qwen3.

release_date.note: The original Qwen README revision dated October 16, 2023 explicitly offers qwen-turbo through DashScope and supplies API onboarding instructions. This establishes availability by that day, materially earlier than the prior catalog date, but the documentation addition does not say the model was launched that day. No primary source establishing its initial launch date was located; later dated alias targets remain distinct.

open_weights.note: Explicitly proprietary; do not substitute an open Qwen checkpoint.

license.note: No open-weight license applies to this proprietary API model; service terms are separate.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 search of English and Chinese developer documentation and Qwen releases found no nominal total size for qwen-turbo / qwen-turbo-2025-04-28. The smaller-size QwQ-32B comparison does not supply a count. No explicit variant or fine-tune relationship to a sized base was found; Qwen3 family membership and similar benchmark language do not justify transferring Qwen3-30B-A3B or another open model size. This null is not based on demanding an exact tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked independently of total size: no nominal activated count, dense/MoE classification or named sized-base lineage is disclosed for the documented Qwen3 Turbo snapshot. Qwen3-30B-A3B has a published 3B active count, but the developer does not identify Turbo with that model. Sparse attention in the older Qwen2.5-Turbo announcement does not establish the later snapshot topology or active-parameter count.

architecture.note: No exact dense/MoE topology is established for the final alias. Open Qwen checkpoint architectures and older sparse-attention details cannot be transferred.

context_window.note: Tokens; corrects the older revision limit.

reasoning.note: Optional thinking mode is explicitly documented.

tool_call.note: Function Calling is explicitly unsupported in both documented regions.

description.value: Proprietary Qwen3 text model with thinking and non-thinking modes; the final qwen-turbo alias matched the 2025-04-28 snapshot.
description.note: Replaces broad workload claims with documented model identity and modes.

patch.description: Proprietary Qwen3 text model with thinking and non-thinking modes; the final qwen-turbo alias matched the 2025-04-28 snapshot.
patch.notes: The documented alias matches qwen-turbo-2025-04-28. Nominal total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed; no sized base-model lineage is identified. Dense/MoE architecture and original alias release date remain unresolved. Alibaba scheduled retirement in Beijing and Singapore for 2026-10-10; endpoint availability was not tested. Fresh repository-history research establishes qwen-turbo API availability by October 16, 2023, but no original launch date is verified.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit leaves total and active counts undisclosed with explicit null patches. Reopened the original English card, proprietary-model documentation and Qwen2.5 releases; added the Chinese exact card, Qwen3 release and current Alibaba release-history page. The alias remains documented as qwen-turbo-2025-04-28. Searches for nominal counts and named-base lineage found only family-level descriptions and a smaller-size comparison with QwQ-32B, insufficient to transfer any open Qwen3 count. Preserved the other prior audited fields and corrections. The release-date re-audit checked original 2023 repository history and developer searches: qwen-turbo was documented as an available API by October 16, 2023, but no dated launch announcement was found. The release date remains null instead of substituting a documentation edit or a later snapshot date.

searches: QwenLM/Qwen README_CN commit history from August through November 2023

accessed_originals.evidence: The October 16, 2023 immutable README names qwen-turbo and qwen-plus as available DashScope hosted APIs, distinguishes their speed/quality and provides API-key onboarding plus SDK installation instructions. It establishes that qwen-turbo existed by October 16, 2023 without claiming an original release date.

The official repository commit is timestamped October 16, 2023. Inspection of earlier October 14 README and this revision locates the documentation addition; a documentation commit timestamp alone does not establish the model launch date.

findings: The original API documentation substantially predates previously checked 2024 quota notices and baseline dates.
The original text describes currently available API options, without an author-dated initial release declaration.
limitations: No primary launch day or month was verified. The by-date is an availability bound and is not placed into release_date.
